bibliographic.title: Preventable yet persistent: silicosis and gaps in public health policy – a narrative review
bibliographic.authors: Rajmane P, Saha R, Devagekar A, Mandati Santhosh Reddy, Revanasiddappa Devarinti
bibliographic.citation_apa: Rajmane, P., Saha, R., Devagekar, A., Reddy, M. S., & Devarinti, R. (2026). Preventable yet persistent: silicosis and gaps in public health policy – a narrative review. Monaldi Archives for Chest Disease. https://doi.org/10.4081/monaldi.2026.3937

methodology.study_design: narrative review of literature on silicosis and occupational/public health policy
methodology.sector: occupational health, public health, pharmacy practice
methodology.technology_context: occupational lung disease (silicosis) prevention, regulatory enforcement, and public health policy; no LLM or conversational AI systems studied

eligibility.exclusion_reason: Narrative review on silicosis and occupational/public health policy accountability; generative AI appears only in a writing-process declaration stating no AI was used. No LLM systems, conversational AI, chatbots, agents, RAG, or AI governance in regulated technology contexts.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Despite Python triage hits on accountability, governance, ethics, legal, healthcare, and AI terms, the article's substantive focus is silicosis epidemiology, prevention, and occupational health policy. Governance and accountability refer to employer/regulatory responsibility for occupational disease, not conversational or LLM governance. AI mentions are limited to a standard publisher declaration of non-use in manuscript preparation.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal reflects the narrative review as an occupational health policy paper, not as evidence for LLM conversational governance. Narrative review design is stated but systematic search/sampling methods are not described in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: For the review scope on conversational governance of LLMs in regulated settings, relevance is very low. Provided text shows a coherent occupational health policy argument but no substantive engagement with LLMs, conversational systems, or AI governance mechanisms.

coding.theme: Occupational health policy and accountability for silicosis prevention
coding.subtheme: Gaps in enforcement, reporting, and inter-sector coordination

synthesis.main_claim: Silicosis is preventable but persists globally due to inconsistent adoption of engineering controls, surveillance, and weak enforcement; the authors advocate rights-based accountability, mandatory digital reporting, and stronger inter-ministerial occupational health governance.
synthesis.contribution: Synthesizes occupational health, epidemiological, legal, and policy literature to argue for a paradigm shift from silicosis management to elimination through coordinated regulatory action.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central evidence on conversational governance of LLMs; keyword overlap on governance/accountability/regulation is contextual to occupational disease policy, not AI systems.

evidence.claim: Article is a narrative review on silicosis and public health policy, not on LLMs or conversational AI.
